summary: Iteration 10 tests whether the lean bracket search strategy (TP={4,8}, max-profile secondaries, budget=2 evals) remains optimal when the workload token distribution changes dramatically — from the default (prompt mean ~512) to 4 named presets (chatbot, contentgen, summarization, multidoc) with 2–20× different prompt lengths, across 2 arrival rates and 2 GPU types (H100, A100-SXM), totaling 16 regimes. This directly stress-tests the workload-agnosticism claim from prior iterations and exposes a known structural blindspot in the model-aware analytical formula.
key_points: h-main: Lean bracket should match global best within 1% on all 8 H100 workload regimes (4 presets × 2 rates). TP=4 is predicted to win 7/8 regimes; TP=8 wins only chatbot at rate=100. Probe-established global bests range from 0.0169 (multidoc) to 0.2687 (chatbot r500). All 5 search seeds must produce identical results per regime (deterministic).

h-control-negative: The model-aware formula (load_index + 400/BW crossover) is predicted to fail on 3/8 H100 regimes (summarization r100, contentgen r100, multidoc r100) because it has no prompt-length input — it predicts TP=8 at rate=100 regardless of workload, but long prompts (≥1024 tokens) shift the actual crossover below rate=100. Expected accuracy: ≤62.5% on H100, ≤50% on A100-SXM. This validates that the lean bracket's advantage is specifically its direct-measurement approach vs. formula-based prediction.

h-robustness: Lean bracket should also match global best within 1% on all 8 A100-SXM regimes, but with different TP winner patterns (e.g., chatbot r500 favors TP=8 on A100-SXM vs TP=4 on H100 due to lower memory bandwidth shifting the crossover rate). The multidoc preset (avg 10240 prompt tokens) is the hardest test — TP=8 wins on A100-SXM due to KV cache capacity constraints at TP=4 that don't appear on H100.

Code change is minimal: extend search_blis_iter8.py with a --workload CLI arg, expand the GLOBAL_BEST_TABLE key to a 5-tuple including workload, and add the model-aware formula as a testable strategy. No changes to BLIS itself.

Confirmation criteria: lean bracket within 1% of global best on all 16 regimes (8 H100 + 8 A100-SXM). Refutation: any regime where lean bracket exceeds 1% gap, or where model-aware formula achieves >62.5% on H100. Key diagnostic: if multidoc at TP=4 shows dropped requests (KV cache OOM), that explains any anomalous TP=8 wins.
